column4: Close-up of the same porcelain maid seen directly from behind, between the shoulder blades, matching the back view of the character reference: her long orange hair parts down the middle of her back and falls to both sides, and her coal dress back shows clearly. In the center of the frame, between the shoulder blades and just above the white apron bow, a small round brass-and-coal collar plate is set into the back: this is where her wind-up key is mounted. Draw only the round mount plate with a short square stub in its center, no key bow (the key is added separately). Flower ornament and coal ribbon visible at the upper right edge. Keep the composition and hair style of the second reference but move the mount down onto the dress between the shoulder blades.

The doll's wind-up key exactly as on her back in the reference: a classic clockwork butterfly key with two round loops joined by a short bar, coal black with a thin orange inner rim, seen perfectly face-on from behind so the two loops are left and right of a small round hub, hub at the exact center of the image, no shaft visible. Nothing else in the image. The entire background is one flat pure chroma green (#00B140).
